summary: Intermittent cross-region egress surge when strict region pin enabled causing p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent spikes in p99 latency for generation requests after they enabled strict region pin (geo residency enforcement).

Impact: Sporadic 400-800ms increases in p99 token latency and occasional streaming disconnects for a subset (~3-5%) of requests. Visible to production traffic for BrightHealth AI on their dedicated pool; customer sees higher tail latency and increased error budget burn.

Environment: Dedicated capacity customer, strict region pin = enabled (strict_failover=true), primary region us-west, failover region us-east, model pinned to redwood-rlhf-13b, prod, observed primarily between 06:00-09:00 PDT and 18:00-19:00 PDT.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer issues a steady stream (200-300 rps) of 1-2k token generation requests to the hosted endpoint with region pin headers set to us-west.
2) At capacity peaks or during short infra fluctuations, some requests are routed across a failover path to us-east despite strict pin being enabled.
3) When cross-region egress occurs, p99 latency increases by ~400-800ms and some streaming sessions disconnect.

Observed behavior:
- Routing logs show multi-hop egress for a subset of pinned requests.
- Autoscaling in dedicated pool reports transient inability to allocate new workers in us-west leading to routing decisions.
- Edge gateway returns 502/streaming disconnect events correlated with cross-region hops.

Expected behavior:
- With strict region pin enabled, requests should either fail-fast or be queued/denied per policy rather than be silently routed cross-region.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- Traces: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/traces?traceId=abc123 (link sent to Eng)
- Dashboard: /dashboards/dedicated/pools/us-west/p99-latency
- Customer-provided sample request IDs: rQ2f8, rQ2f9, rQ3a2 (timestamps included in attached log snippet).

Temporary workaround requested/used:
- Support suggested toggling strict_failover=false to allow failover routing until root cause fixed. Customer applied and saw immediate reduction in p99 spikes but is concerned about data residency implications.

Request: Root cause analysis of why strict pin is not preventing cross-region egress, and recommendation for a fix that preserves residency guarantees or an approved safe workaround that meets compliance needs.
investigation_notes:
03/10 Support triage: Assigned to Marcus Chen. Confirmed customer is on Dedicated and has strict_failover flag set.
03/11 SRE initial check: No recent config changes to region pinning service. Noted increased worker churn in us-west cluster between 06:00-09:00 and 18:00-19:00 PDT.
03/12 Networking: Found transient BGP flap reported in us-west provider peering (ticket #NET-901). Possible multi-path NAT causing egress rewrite.
03/13 Routing team: Identified race in routing policy evaluation where strict_failover fallback path check runs after capacity-aware routing; if local pool returns a transient capacity error, fallback code path executes and may select cross-region egress without honoring strict residency header.
03/14 Hypothesis: Combination of transient capacity error + race condition in policy evaluation allowed routes to be selected that bypassed strict residency enforcement before enforcement flags were re-evaluated.
Investigative artifacts: logs uploaded to /support/archives/SUP-87203/logs.tar.gz, debug traces in telemetry, and a short reproducer script created by Eng (internal PR linked).
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged ticket to customer and requested example request IDs and timestamps. Asked for API key scope and whether headers include 'x-redwood-region-pin'.
Customer (BrightHealth AI - Daniel Park) 2026-03-10: Provided request IDs and confirmed header usage; said toggle strict_failover=false reduces latency but is not acceptable long term for compliance.
SRE (Ravi Singh) 2026-03-11: Noted autoscaler logs show several scale-up failures in us-west due to pod boot timeout; filing infra ticket NET-901 for cloud provider peering flap.
Routing Eng (Lina Morales) 2026-03-12: Reproduced route selection race in internal testbed; created PR to reorder enforcement checks (see related_github_prs).

Support (Marcus Chen) 2026-03-13: Communicated temporary workaround to customer and scheduled a 1:1 sync to review compliance implications. Asked customer to hold off on toggling back until a safe plan is in place.
Customer (Daniel Park) 2026-03-14: Requests ETA for permanent fix and asks whether audit logs will show any cross-region egress during the incident window for compliance review.
resolution: Workaround provided: advised customer to keep strict_failover=false only for a controlled short window if they accept the tradeoff. Engineering rolled a bugfix PR to reorder residency enforcement and capacity checks; change has passed unit tests and is staged for canary deploy to routing cluster in us-west. Next steps: canary rollout (canary targets 5% traffic) then monitor p99 for 48 hours. If no regression, promote to prod. Also adding an audit flag to log when requests are routed cross-region while strict pin is true.
